tagline: Under the Spanish Peaks and down the Purgatoire, tall tales included.
intro: Highway 12 leaves US 160 north of La Veta and runs south through town into the San Isabel National Forest, through Cuchara near the Spanish Peaks and over Cucharas Pass at 9,995 feet. Beyond Monument Park it turns east near Stonewall Gap and follows the Purgatoire River down past Weston and Cokedale, a former coal mining town, to Trinidad. The red rock walls of the Dakota Wall and the Devil's Stairsteps belong to the same country.

The legends are the local kind: whether George Simpson saved Trinidad from the Utes by distracting them with taunts, and what became of Juan Humana and his conquistadors, who vanished near the Purgatoire in 1594. The state's byway page promises no answers.

moments.title: La Veta
moments.text: Named for a mineral vein, the town began with Francisco Fort, a 100-foot-square adobe with two-foot walls and gun ports along the parapets, attacked by Utes in 1863.

moments.title: Spanish Peaks
moments.text: The Comanche name means double mountain, and both summits stand higher than any point farther east in the United States, the first sight of the Rockies on the Santa Fe Trail.

moments.title: Stonewall Gap
moments.text: The Middle Fork of the Purgatoire cuts a gap through 8,400-foot Stonewall Ridge here, and the highway leads east down the river valley 33 miles to Trinidad.

practical: The 35-mile extension over 11,248-foot Cordova Pass is partly gravel and closed in winter; the Forest Service does not usually plow it, so it is normally impassable from mid-November to late May.

sources.label: Colorado Department of Transportation, Highway of Legends
